cues: Warm phenol with chloroform and sodium hydroxide at sixty to seventy degrees.
The alkali pulls hydrogen chloride out of chloroform, creating dichlorocarbene, a neutral carbon with only six electrons.
It is electron hungry, a weak electrophile.
text: The Reimer Tiemann reaction. Warm phenol with chloroform and sodium hydroxide at sixty to seventy degrees. The alkali pulls hydrogen chloride out of chloroform, creating dichlorocarbene, a neutral carbon with only six electrons. It is electron hungry, a weak electrophile.
